title: A message or email that got no reply for a long time
titleVi: Tin nhắn / email lâu không được hồi âm
bullets: whether you finally received the reply
and explain how you felt about the experience

notes.label: Who
notes.text: Ms. Lan, founder of a craft-export company

notes.label: About
notes.text: my hat idea; 10 minutes' advice; shadow her team

notes.label: Reply?
notes.text: yes, after 5½ weeks + a follow-up; trade fair in Europe

segments.v: I want to talk about an email I sent to Ms. Lan a few months ago. She has a company that sells handmade products from craft villages to other countries. I wanted to ask her for some advice about my business idea. I also asked if I could visit her company in the summer. I wrote the email very carefully. After I sent it, I waited but she didn't reply. I checked my email every day. I felt worried and disappointed. I thought maybe she didn't like my email. After five weeks, I sent another short email. She replied the next day. She said she was very busy because she went to Europe. She invited me to visit her company. I felt very happy. I learned that I should not give up too early.

fluency.band9: Who and why → how the email came about → what it asked → emotional timeline (first week, third week, five and a half weeks) → the reply → reflection with two lessons.

lexical.band9: on the spur of the moment, shadow, drafting, presumptuous, put her off, follow-up, trade fair, backlog, rollercoaster.

grammar.band6: Error: “because she went to Europe” (she'd been at a trade fair in Europe).
grammar.band9: Past perfect (I'd read an interview; she'd been at a trade fair), past perfect with “started” (By the third week, I'd started to assume…), modal perfect (mistakes that might have put her off), and third conditional (If I'd given up, I'd have missed…).

analysis.keyDifference: Band 6 error: “because she went to Europe” should be past perfect (“she'd been in Europe”). Band 9 shows the emotional timeline (first week → third week → five and a half weeks), explains the ending, and uses a third conditional to reflect.
